As an IT SPECIALIST (DATA MANAGEMENT)-TITLE 32, GS-2210-11, you will provide expert technical advice, guidance, and recommendations on critical data-related issues. Provide guidance to program stakeholders on the application of data categorization, privacy, and retention in accordance with regulations and policies.

Define responsibilities related to data governance and ensure accountability for stewardship of the Command's principal information assets. Develop procedural guidance for data ownership, access control, data management, and data manipulation to manage and administer organizational data.

Work with personnel responsible for database administration, data management, data modeling, data governance, data retention, data masking, corporate reporting, application data refreshes and Security Technical Implementation Guidelines compliance. Serve as a point of escalation for governance, data quality and protection issues.

Facilitate development and implementation of data quality standards, data protection standards and adoption requirements. Define indicators of performance and quality metrics and ensure compliance with data related policies, standards, roles and responsibilities, and adoption requirements.

Design and develop integrative views of data to enable informed decision making. Conduct analyses to ensure architecture and standards support, metadata management, financial auditability, process reengineering, system modernization and investment management.

Collaborate with infrastructure engineers, software developers, Enterprise Data Architects, system owners, and business users to understand the end-to-end lifecycle of data. Coordinate planning, development, implementation, and administration of systems for the acquisition, storage, and retrieval of data tailored to changing customer requirements.

Develop and administer data standards, policies, and procedures. Design data visualization and reporting solutions to support informed decision making for organizational initiatives. Perform other duties as assigned.

A more comprehensive detailed description of the position may be found in Position Description PDD2530P01 on file in the employing unit or in the Human Resources Office. Contact the KY HRO Staffing Section via email for additional information, ng.ky.kyarng.mbx.hro-technician-staffing@army.mil.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENT: Experience that has provided a basic knowledge of data processing functions and general management principles that enabled the applicant to understand the stages required to automate a work process.

Experience may have been gained in work such as computer operator or assistant, computer sales representative, program analyst, or other positions that required the use or adaptation of computer programs and systems. Must have Security+ Certification.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Must have at least 36 months experience that approaches techniques and requirements appropriate to an assigned computer applications area or computer specialty area in an organization.

Experience planning the sequence of actions necessary to accomplish the assignment where this entailed coordination with others outside the organizational unit and development of project controls. Experience that required adaptations of guidelines or precedents to meet the needs of the assignment.

Experience preparing documentation on cost/benefit studies where is involved summarizing the material and organizing it in a logical fashion. EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: Resume must have complete dates, work schedule, and/or hours worked per week for both civilian and military employment.

(Example: 2 JAN 1980 to 3 MAR 1981; 0800-1630 M-F or JAN 1980 to MAR 1981; 40 hrs/wk) Use of year only and unspecified work schedule will result in disqualification.

Each applicant must fully substantiate -in their own words- that they meet 100% of the minimum requirements and specialized experience listed above in detail; otherwise, the applicant will be considered unqualified for this position. Do NOT copy and paste from the vacancy announcement or the position description.

Also, make sure the applicant's name is on every document submitted, otherwise it will NOT be considered.

As a Supervisory IT Specialist (INFOSEC), you will perform the following duties: Oversee the procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of a Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) system in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-12.

Conduct system security evaluation and ensure the rigorous application of information security and information assurance policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of all Information Technology (IT) services.

Conduct risk and vulnerability assessment of planned and installed information systems to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and protection needs. Apply the Risk Management Framework (RMF) as it applies to Federal Information Systems and analyze and determine the Risk Mitigation process.

Perform a full range of supervisory functions, including developing and evaluating performance standards, giving advice, counsel, or instruction to employees. Make or approve selections for subordinate positions and identify training needs.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS: Applicants must possess the following two certifications: A current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), also known as (ISC)2, AND a Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) Certified Incident Handler (GCIH).

Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) is an independent information security certification granted by the International Information System Security Certification Consortium, also known as (ISC)2 Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) The GIAC Incident Handler certification validates a practitioner's ability to detect, respond, and resolve computer security incidents using a wide range of essential security skills.

GCIH certification holders have the knowledge needed to manage security incidents by understanding common attack techniques, vectors and tools, as well as defend against and respond to such attacks when they occur. Incumbent must have a current or past System Owner designation of a Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) system.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENTS: Ship sailing and aircraft flight time supporting platform IT infrastructure, applications, or sensor instrumentation during mission operations. This position will be filled under the DOC Alternative Personnel System (CAPS). Under CAPS, positions are classified by career, pay plan, and pay band.

You will serve as a SUPERVISORY INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SPECIALIST (INFOSEC), located in the Security Manager (N00SM) of Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station, Pacific (NCTAMS PAC).
You will serve as the expert leading the planning, implementation, and evaluation of Information, Personnel, Physical, Industrial, and Communication Security, alongside Antiterrorism/Force Protection and Information Assurance.
You will serve as the technical and analytical expert for all aspects of the Security Program for NCTAMS PAC and its Region.
You will plan, evaluate and execute a comprehensive security program encompassing all facets for security management, with protecting the various networks in the NCTAMS PAC Area of Responsibility (AOR) as the paramount focus.
You will establish security programs to meet requirements for NCTAMS PAC departments, components and regional activities, taking into consideration the needs of mission objectives, operation requirements, and personnel interests.
You will perform strategic planning, workforce planning, resource management, knowledge management, and auditing to ensure program compliance and operational readiness.
You will serve as the security expert and consultant for NCTAMS PAC and its region.
You will participate as a voting member in the development of new tools/systems, Navy policy and methods at the Department of the Navy, Chief Information Officer Information Assurance/Computer Network Defense Top 10 Focus Working Group.
You will provide local and regional oversight on the certification and accreditation of all networks in the NCTAMS PAC area of responsibility.
You will develop long-range plans for IT security systems that anticipate, identify, evaluate, mitigate, and minimize risks associated with IT systems vulnerabilities.
You will serve as the principal advisor and representative to the Commanding Officer and Chief of Staff Officer on all matters of Communications Security/Electronic Key Management System.
You will plan and establish Security Department work objectives, and ensure completed work is timely and accurate.
You will act as Commanding Officer’s representative in granting, denying, revoking, suspending or restricting security clearances.

The duties and responsibilities for a Supervisory IT Specialist GS-2210-14 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Serves as a Supervisory IT Specialist with responsibility for directing and managing enterprise information technology services, including customer support, network operations, communication systems, and systems administration.

Provides oversight of end-user computing services, including desktop systems, laptops, mobile devices, peripherals, and telecommunications services. Monitors systems administration activities to ensure reliability, availability, and security of enterprise systems.

Develops, implements, and maintains IT policies, procedures, and operational standards. Plans and assigns work based on priorities and employee capabilities and establish performance standards and evaluate employee's performance.
To qualify for the position of Supervisory IT Specialist, at GS-2210-14, you must meet the qualification requirements listed below. Basic Qualifications (2210 series): Please refer to the OPM IT Management Series 2210 Qualification Standard for the specific experience requirements for the GS-12 and above positions.

AND Specialized Experience: To qualify for the GS-14 grade level, you must have one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service, or comparable non-Federal experience.

Specialized experience is defined as experience performing the following duties: Providing guidance in developing, implementing, and updating policies, procedures, and operational standards pertaining to IT network operations, service functions, communication systems, and systems administration; Planning workflow and work assignments for staff by setting and adjusting short-term work priorities; Monitoring system performance and leading corrective actions to enhance performance and prevent future issues; Advising on new and advanced technologies and determining the impact on operational effectiveness; and Managing the full lifecycle of enterprise-level IT systems, overseeing the planning, installation, configuration, and maintenance of hardware and software.

You MUST meet all qualification requirements, including time-in-grade, by 07/27/2026 of this announcement. Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating.

See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume.

The Supervisory Information Technology Specialist (Quality Lead) is in the build workstream solution layer and defines and enforces the program's test strategy, quality gates, and readiness evidence so delivery pods can ship usable, supportable increments with predictable quality.

The incumbent standardizes cross-pod quality practices, validates that acceptance criteria are testable and met, and drives release readiness across environments and integrated capabilities.

The incumbent must be familiar with performance, security, and contract testing patterns for enterprise APIs and distributed services; and possess proven stakeholder management skills across product, engineering, architecture, security, data, and operations to resolve quality risks quickly.

The duties of the position include, but are not limited to: Driving the strategic product vision, roadmap, and prioritization to deliver business outcomes in alignment with program release plans.

Designing and executing the end-to-end test strategy across units, including integration, regression, and user acceptance testing aligned to the build delivery cadence and release trains.

Establishing and running quality gates and readiness evidence requirements for sprint and program increment completion, including defect thresholds and sign-off criteria.

Partnering with product owners and delivery leads to ensure requirements are traceable end-to-end from requirement to epic to story to test coverage and completion evidence prior to acceptance. Driving integrated testing across pods by coordinating test planning, test data needs, environment readiness, and cross-pod dependency validation.

Driving defect management standards and triage rhythms and ensuring issues are prioritized, routed, and resolved with clear accountability and cross-pod visibility. Leading release readiness validation, including performance, security, and contract/API testing expectations in coordination with PAX, security, and data counterparts.

Providing quality risk reporting and escalation inputs into program governance and ensuring leaders have actionable quality signals and mitigation plans. Driving requirements-to-test traceability across pods, including coverage reporting and evidence linking for sprint, program increment, and release readiness.

Driving the program test tooling strategy and administration, including test management, automated testing frameworks, reporting dashboards, and CI/CD quality gate integration.

Running the quality chapter cadence (standards, templates, playbooks, and peer reviews), including test tooling workflows, quality gate configurations, and requirements-to-test traceability conventions and reporting.

Deploying and enabling designated quality representatives across pods, coaching teams on test tooling adoption and automation practices, and verifying traceability evidence and adherence to agreed guardrails and gates.

As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be a trusted technical advisor to GitLab’s largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, helping them avoid operational disruption and get the most from GitLab.

You’ll combine deep Linux systems expertise, GitLab and CI/CD knowledge, and a proactive support mindset to understand each customer’s environment, anticipate and prevent issues, and solve complex technical and business challenges.

In a typical week, you might be prioritizing strategic blockers with customer stakeholders, partnering with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to drive defect resolution and influence the roadmap, or diving into code, logs, and tools like strace to troubleshoot performance issues.

Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.

Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.
Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.
Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.
Collaborate with Product , Development , Infrastructure , Customer Success , and Sales teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.
Act as a technical expert on GitLab and CI/CD implementations, advising customers on how incidents and service interruptions impact their workflows and how to mitigate them.
Create and improve support content, including documentation and knowledge articles, to help customers and GitLab team members resolve issues more efficiently.
Partner closely with Support Engineering team members through pairing sessions and stable counterpart relationships to share knowledge and solve problems together.
Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.

Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.
Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.
Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.
Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.
Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.
Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.
Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.
Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.

The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most from GitLab by troubleshooting complex issues and digging into code and logs to understand why something is not working as expected.

As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be part of our broader Support Engineering organization, working closely with other Support Engineers through regular pairing sessions, 1:1s, coffee chats, and Slack conversations to stay connected while collaborating asynchronously across time zones.

We balance autonomy with accountability, giving you flexibility to structure your shift in a way that fits your life while ensuring we can reliably address customer issues. Thanks to GitLab’s Transparency value, you can see what we are working on in our Support Team page.

Additionally, you can see our company roadmap and meetings to see what we are working on at any time.

Speaks and writes in a clear, concise, organized, and convincing manner that is appropriate to the audience. Facilitates an open exchange of ideas to ensure all group input is considered. Handles technical, sensitive, or controversial topics with agility involving executives/managers as appropriate.

Problem Solving: Identifies and analyzes problems, weighs relevance and accuracy of information, generates and evaluates alternative solutions, and makes sound recommendations.

Your resume must be no more than two (2) pages and should clearly demonstrate how your experience aligns with the responsibilities and specialized experience required for this position. Do not copy language directly from the vacancy announcement, as you will be deemed ineligible for consideration.
